The first sound-film adaptation of Hanns Heinz Ewers’s novel: a fanatical scientist, after creating artificial animals, fashions a synthetic human — „Alraune“ — from the bodies of a hanged man and a prostitute; the cold-hearted woman then takes cruel revenge on her „creator,“ who has fallen hopelessly in love with her. Cast: Brigitte Helm, Albert Bassermann, Harald Paulsen, Adolf E. Licho, Agnes Straub, Bernhard Goetzke. German premiere 2 March 1930 (per the Illustrierter Film-Kurier listing). Marks Kaper’s earliest film work.

records.title: Rhein- und Ruhr-Zeitung, 10 December 1929 — Jazz auf vier Flügeln review
records.description: Review titled 'Jazz auf vier Flügeln — Zweites städtisches Sonderkonzert in Hamborn' (signed Dr. Funk) in the Rhein- und Ruhr-Zeitung, 10 December 1929. It covers the First Piano Quartet (Erstes Klavier-Quartett) of four pianists — Bronisław Kaper, Leopold Mittmann, Alexander Zakin and Julian Pomeranc — performing on four grand pianos, including their own compositions. The programme ranged from Schubert, Verdi, Strauss, Kreisler and Rimsky-Korsakov to the 'Blue Danube' and modern dances; Kaper contributed a tango for four grand pianos (Vierflügeltango), and Mittmann a Jazz-Prélude and three 'Jazz-Babies'.

records.altText: Newspaper clipping reporting that Walter Jurmann and Bronisław Kaper were preparing to leave New York for MGM in California.

records.title: Koszutski Girls in Teatr “Perskie Oko”: przegląd rewji (1926)
records.description: Page 8 of the illustrated programme Teatr “Perskie Oko”: przegląd rewji (Warsaw, 1926), with three ensemble photographs labeled “Koszutski-Girls.” The image provides visual context for the troupe named in Kaper’s 1923 manuscript; it does not document the manuscript’s authorship or the “Mus. B. Asper” inscription.
